Charles Lindbergh (February 4, 1902 - August 26, 1974) was an American aviator, military officer, and author.

Cuban Revolution was the military and political movement that overthrew the dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista, who had ruled Cuba from 1952 to 1959.

Enoch is a biblical figure and patriarch prior to Noah's flood.

Georgia's reformist president for two terms after 2004, this jurist later turned up across the border as governor of Ukraine's Odesa Oblast — who is he?
He seized Libya in a bloodless 1969 coup and ruled for over four decades as 'Brotherly Leader' until rebels overthrew him in 2011 — who was he?
Muammar Gaddafi: Leader of Libya from 1969 to 2011. Initially ideologically committed to Arab nationalism and Arab socialism, Gaddafi later ruled according to his own Third International Theory.
More than just nudism, this lifestyle and movement frames non-sexual social nudity around harmony with nature and respect for the environment — what is it called?
Naturism: Practice and advocacy of social nudity.
Codenamed Operation Neptune and preceded by the elaborate deception Operation Bodyguard, this June 6, 1944 assault is the largest seaborne invasion in history — by what more common name is it known?
Normandy landings: World War II landing operation in Europe.
After resigning as Germany's finance minister within six months of taking office, this politician later co-founded a left-wing party opposing his former party's reforms — who is he?
Forced out of school at ten by poverty, this future Chinese general rose from private second class to become Minister of National Defense from 1954 to 1959 — who was he?
Peng Dehuai: Chinese politician and general (1898–1974)

Ruling Mexico for more than three decades until his 1911 overthrow, this general-turned-dictator once studied for the priesthood before switching to law under the mentorship of future president Benito Juárez. Who is he?
Porfirio Díaz: President and Dictator of Mexico from 1876 to 1911.
A trained psychiatrist who became the first president of Republika Srpska, he spent twelve years as a fugitive before being convicted of genocide by a UN tribunal — who is he?
Radovan Karadžić: Bosnian Serb politician and war criminal (born 1945)
This Congress politician led his party to victory in the 2023 election and became the second Chief Minister of Telangana — who is he?
Revanth Reddy: Chief Minister of Telangana (born 1969)
Raised in Russian-ruled Poland in a secular Jewish family, this Marxist theorist co-founded the anti-war Spartacus League and is remembered as a champion of socialist democracy — who is she?
Venerated as a prophet across three major faiths, this biblical figure guided Israel's transition from the age of judges to kingship, first anointing Saul and later David — who is he?
Born to a poor Cossack family and later a close ally of Stalin, this Soviet cavalry commander founded the Red Cavalry and became the subject of patriotic songs — who is he?
Only the second person to complete a full five-year term as Chief Minister of Karnataka, this Congress politician also served two stints as the state's Deputy Chief Minister — who is he?
Siddaramaiah: Chief Minister of Karnataka from 2013 to 2018 and 2023 to 2026.

Defined by a one-man police state, forced agricultural collectivization, and a sweeping cult of personality, this set of Soviet policies held sway from 1927 until the dictator's death in 1953 — what is it called?
Stalinism: Political and economic policies implemented by Joseph Stalin.

Widely regarded as one of the greatest Roman historians, this writer chronicled the empire from Augustus's death to Domitian's reign in two major works, and also penned an account of his general father-in-law's campaigns in Britain — who was he?

Fought entirely on Carthaginian soil after King Masinissa's repeated raids provoked a doomed counterattack under Hasdrubal, which 149-146 BC conflict was the last and final clash between Rome and Carthage?
Third Punic War: War between Rome and Carthage (149–146 BC). The war was fought entirely within Carthaginian territory, in what is now northern Tunisia.
A legendary tenth-year siege in Greek mythology, sparked when Paris took Helen from her husband—immortalized in Homer's Iliad and Odyssey—what's this ancient conflict?
Trojan War: Legendary war in Greek mythology. The Trojan War was a legendary conflict in Greek mythology that took place around the thirteenth century or early twelfth century BC.
Born to a murdered Arvernian aristocrat, this Gallic chieftain united the tribes of Gaul in a doomed revolt against Julius Caesar's legions — who was he?
This Kenyan activist founded the tree-planting Green Belt Movement and in 2004 became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize. Who was she?
Called the 'father of modern Liberia,' he was the country's longest-serving president, drawing foreign investment and pursuing national unification from 1944 until his death in 1971 — who is he?
William Tubman: President of Liberia from 1944 to 1971. William Vacanarat Shadrach Tubman (29 November 1895 – 23 July 1971) was a Liberian politician.
A labour lawyer and longtime Communist Party member, which Spanish politician founded the left-wing alliance Sumar and serves as Second Deputy Prime Minister?
Yolanda Díaz: Spanish politician and lawyer (born 1971)
Who among these was born first?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four. After helping found Shu Han, Zhuge Liang exercised near-total authority over both civil and military affairs.
Which of these four is the oldest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
SQL (published 1986) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Laura Bassi is a physicist. Laura Maria Caterina Bassi Veratti (29 October 1711 – 20 February 1778) was an Italian physicist and academic.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Antoine Lavoisier is a chemist. It is generally accepted that Lavoisier's great accomplishments in chemistry stem largely from his changing the science from a qualitative to a quantitative one.
What is the atomic number of Nitrogen?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
In what year was Robert F. Kennedy Jr. born?
Robert F. Kennedy Jr.: A member of the prominent Kennedy family, he is a son of Senator and US attorney general Robert F.
In what year was William Howard Taft born?
William Howard Taft: Taft attended Yale and joined Skull and Bones, of which his father was a founding member.
In what year was Terry Gou born?
Terry Gou: Terry Guo (Chinese: 郭台銘; pinyin: Guō Táimíng; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Koeh Tâi-bêng; born 18 October 1950) is a Taiwanese billionaire businessman and politician.
In what year did Jerry Buss die?
Jerry Buss: Gerald Hatten Buss (January 27, 1933 – February 18, 2013) was an American businessman, investor, chemist, and philanthropist.
In what year did Fritz Haber die?
Fritz Haber: For this work, Haber has been called one of the most important scientists and industrial chemists in human history.
In what year was Proxima Centauri discovered?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
In what year was Bromine discovered?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.

Gabapentin: Pfizer. Gabapentin is a
central nervous system (CNS) depressant and derivative of the inhibitory neurotransmitter, GABA.
Which country is Focke-Wulf Fw 190 from?
Focke-Wulf Fw 190: Germany. Along with its well-known counterpart, the Messerschmitt Bf 109, the Fw 190 became the backbone of the Jagdwaffe (Fighter Force) of the Luftwaffe.
Who is credited with discovering Barium?
Barium: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
Who is credited with discovering Lawrencium?
Lawrencium: Albert Ghiorso. Lawrencium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lr (formerly Lw) and atomic number 103.
Who is credited with discovering Francium?
Francium: Marguerite Perey. Francium is a chemical element; it has symbol Fr and atomic number 87.

Sometimes called a nerve impulse or 'spike,' this rapid rise and fall of voltage across a cell membrane ripples to neighboring spots and fires in neurons, muscle cells, and even some plant cells. What is it?
Action potential (also known as a nerve impulse or "spike" when in a neuron) is a series of quick changes in voltage across a cell membrane.
These tropical arachnids are nicknamed 'whip-spiders,' yet they spin no silk and carry no venom — their name actually means 'blunt tail.' Which order are they?
Amblypygi is an order of arachnids also known as whip-spiders or tailless whip-scorpions, not to be confused with whip-scorpions or vinegaroons that belong to the related order Uropygi.
This lustrous grey metalloid, found mainly in the mineral stibnite, was historically powdered for use as a cosmetic known by its Arabic name, kohl. What element is it?
Antimony is a chemical element with the symbol Sb (from Latin stibium) and atomic number 51.

Distinguished from celestial mechanics by asking what heavenly bodies ARE rather than where they are, this science applies physics and chemistry to the Sun, stars, galaxies, and exoplanets — which discipline?
Astrophysics is a science that applies the methods and principles of physics and chemistry in the study of astronomical objects and phenomena including the universe.
Strawberries, blackcurrants and blueberries all count in the kitchen sense — though botanists would object, since the culinary meaning of this word differs from the scientific one. What word?
Berry is a small, pulpy, and often edible fruit.
Caused by a toxin that thrives in low-oxygen conditions — the same one sold cosmetically as 'botox' — this rare illness brings blurred vision and creeping paralysis but rarely a fever. What is it?
Botulism is a rare and potentially fatal illness caused by botulinum toxin (commonly referred to as botox), which is produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.
This worldwide family of over 5,000 fly species — found everywhere except the Antarctic and Arctic — includes the biting midges also known as sand flies — what is it called?
Ceratopogonidae is a family of flies colloquially known as no-see-ums, sand flies, or biting midges, generally 1-3 millimetres (116-18 in) in length.
An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned what he learned there into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen-food industry. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye (December 9, 1886 - October 7, 1956) was an American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist, who is widely considered the founder of the modern frozen food industry.
Thanks to variations in the OR6A2 gene, some people taste this Mediterranean herb as fresh and citrusy while others swear it tastes like soap — its leaves are called cilantro in the US. What is it?
Coriander is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.

This American nuclear physicist worked on the Manhattan Project and later led the Federation of American Scientists, best remembered for his 1959 testimony that helped sink a controversial cabinet nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill (November 11, 1919 - December 14, 2008) was an American nuclear physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project during World War II and was head of the Federation of American Scientists.
This waterfowl belongs to the same family as swans and geese, but is generally smaller and shorter-necked — and despite the shared family, swans and geese don't count as one. What is it?
Duck is the common name for numerous species of waterfowl in the family Anatidae.

Named for Latin words meaning 'within the cytoplasm' and 'little net,' this eukaryotic cell organelle handles protein folding and comes in rough and smooth varieties, forming an interconnected network of membrane-enclosed sacs — name this organelle?
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a part of a transportation system of the eukaryotic cell, and has many other important functions such as protein folding.
Every member of this mammal family is an obligate carnivore with retractile claws and a powerful bite, from forest dwellers to desert hunters — which family is it?
Felidae is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.
Co-author of 'The Communist Manifesto' and lifelong collaborator with Karl Marx, this German theorist finished the second and third volumes of 'Das Kapital' after his partner's death — who is he?
Friedrich Engels (28 November 1820 - 5 August 1895) was a German philosopher, social and political theorist, journalist, businessman, and revolutionary socialist.

Colorless, odorless, and oddly sweet, this viscous sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of every triglyceride in animal fat, and moonlights as a food sweetener — what is it?
Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.

Element 108's isotope 270 carries magic numbers of protons and neutrons that shore it up against fission, yet the most stable forms last only about ten seconds — which synthetic superheavy element is it?
Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.

This broad academic category studies human society, culture, and its fundamental questions — during the Renaissance, the term specifically meant the study of classical literature and language as a secular alternative to religious studies. Name the category?
Humanities are academic disciplines that study aspects of human society and culture, including certain fundamental questions asked by humans.

According to Alfred Adler, this persistent psychological feeling of being deficient compared to others — often rooted in childhood upbringing or social status — can drive a person to overcompensate. Name the concept?
Inferiority complex is a consistent feeling of inadequacy, often resulting in the belief that one is in some way deficient, or inferior, to others.
This self-described 'constitutional law attorney' joined Trump's inner circle in November 2019, though reporters found she'd never argued a federal case — who is she?
Jenna Ellis (born November 1, 1984) is an American conservative suspended lawyer who was a member of Donald Trump's 2020 re-election campaign's legal team.
The world's longest venomous snake with an average length of 3.18 to 4 meters, endemic to Asia and widely distributed though not commonly encountered. What is it?
King cobra (Ophiophagus hannah) is a species complex of snakes endemic to Asia.
This leafy member of the daisy family is eaten raw in salads and sandwiches, though one Asian variety, celtuce, is grown instead for its edible stem — what is it?
Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) is an annual plant of the family Asteraceae mostly grown as a leaf vegetable.
Often caused by cigarette smoking or inhaled chemicals damaging airway cell DNA, this malignant tumor often shows no symptoms until it has already spread. What disease is it?
Lung cancer is a malignant tumor that originates in the tissues of the lungs.

In 1835 she and Caroline Herschel became the first female Honorary Members of the Royal Astronomical Society, and decades later this Scottish polymath's name topped John Stuart Mill's women's-suffrage petition. Who is she?
Mary Somerville (ne Fairfax, formerly Greig; 1780-1872) was a Scottish scientist, writer, and polymath.

An advanced modification of the Korean War-era MiG-15, this Soviet transonic fighter jet entered production in 1952, was license-built in both China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — what's the aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17 (NATO reporting name: Fresco) is a transonic fighter aircraft that was produced in the Soviet Union from 1952 and was operated by air forces internationally.
Caused by antibodies blocking acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, this autoimmune disease most often weakens the muscles of the eyes, face and throat — which disease?
Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a long-term neuromuscular junction disease that leads to varying degrees of skeletal muscle weakness.

Considered primary if a child has never had a long dry stretch, this common childhood condition — usually a developmental delay rather than an illness — is commonly called bedwetting. What's its clinical name?
Nocturnal enuresis (NE), also informally called bedwetting, is involuntary urination while asleep after the age at which bladder control usually begins.
All 14 species of this slim-bodied, dense-furred mammal are semiaquatic, and they're famous for playful antics like sliding into the water and juggling stones — what is it?
Otter are carnivorous mammals in the subfamily Lutrinae.
Favored by royalty in the Chinese Imperial court, this toy dog breed originated in China's ancient capital — name the breed?
Pekingese (also spelled Pekinese) is a breed of toy dog, originating in China.
When this domesticated mammal reached Europe from the Near East, it interbred so freely with local wild boar that scholars still argue whether it's a distinct species — what animal is it?
Pig (Sus domesticus), also called swine (pl.: swine) or hog, is an omnivorous, domesticated, even-toed, hoofed mammal.
A staple food across the world, this tuber is actually an underground stem from a plant in the nightshade family, with wild relatives growing from the southern U.S. all the way to Chile. What is it?
Potato is a starchy tuberous vegetable native to the Americas that is consumed as a staple food in many parts of the world.
Its common side effects read like a list of trade-offs — sedation, weight gain, dry mouth — yet many take this atypical antipsychotic simply to fall asleep — which medication?
Quetiapine (kwi-), sold under the brand name Seroquel among others, is an atypical antipsychotic medication used in the treatment of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder.
He'd spent years building and selling theremins toward a Cornell physics PhD before unveiling, in 1964, the first commercial instrument of its kind — which American electronics pioneer was this?
Robert Moog (MOHG; May 23, 1934 - August 21, 2005) was an American electronics engineer and electronic music pioneer.
This systematic discipline builds testable explanations about nature and society, and is continuously challenged and validated by the community that practices it. What is it?
Science is a systematic discipline that builds and organises knowledge in the form of testable explanations about nature and society.
This spiny thistle species has distinctive red-to-purple flowers and shiny, pale green mottled leaves, and is a fairly typical member of the daisy family — what plant is it?
Silybum marianum is a species of thistle.
This Polish-American Manhattan Project mathematician dreamed up the Monte Carlo method, the cellular automaton, and the design behind thermonuclear weapons — who was he?
Stanisław Ulam (13 April 1909 - 13 May 1984) was a Polish and, later an American mathematician who made important contributions in advancing the understanding of nuclear physics and computer science.

This medical term describes a resting heart rate above 100 beats per minute in adults, which can be either a normal exercise response or a sign of an electrical problem in the heart — what's the condition called?
Tachycardia is a heart rate that exceeds the normal resting rate.

One of five genera in the mackerel family whose members are collectively called tunas, this genus contains eight species, including the Atlantic bluefin, which can grow up to 15 feet long — name this genus?
Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
The two major groups of these reptiles, side-necked and hidden-necked, differ in how they pull in the head — and they breathe air despite many living in water. What animal?
Turtle (order Testudines) are reptiles characterized by a special shell developed mainly from their ribs, as well as keratinized toothless beak.

Its small molecule packs a surprising punch: strong polarity, relentless hydrogen bonding, and a starring role as the fluid of all known life and the main stuff of Earth's oceans — what compound is it?
Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O.

First identified in 1789 and not manufactured at scale until the 1920s, this corrosion-resistant, silvery-grey metal resembles hafnium and takes its name from the mineral that remains its main source — what element, symbol Zr, is it?
Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.
Produced by oxidizing adrenaline and named for its deep violet color, this compound was studied in the mid-20th century as a possible cause of schizophrenia — what is it?
Adrenochrome: Chemical compound. It was the subject of limited research from the 1950s through to the 1970s as a potential cause of schizophrenia.
This Austrian psychotherapist broke from Freud's circle to found 'individual psychology,' emphasizing birth order and coining the term 'inferiority complex' — who was he?
Named after a French physicist considered a father of electromagnetism, this SI base unit measures electric current and equals one coulomb per second — which unit?
Ampere: SI base unit of electric current. The ampere (symbol: A), often shortened to amp, is the unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).
NATO code-named 'Condor,' this Soviet-designed four-engine giant is the largest military transport aircraft still flying today — which aircraft?

Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Soviet military transport aircraft. Assembly of the first aircraft begun in 1979; the An-124 (which was sometimes referred to as the An-40 in the West) performed its maiden flight on 24 December 1982.
This American psychiatrist and pharmaceutical marketer amassed the world's largest personal collection of Chinese art, later donated to the Smithsonian — who is he?
Arthur M. Sackler: American physician and executive (1913–1987)
Sold under the brand name Lioresal, this muscle relaxant treats spasticity from spinal cord injuries or MS and is sometimes used off-label for alcohol withdrawal — what is it?
Baclofen: Gabapentinoid and Skeletal Muscle Relaxant.

With his former teacher Alfred North Whitehead, this English philosopher co-wrote Principia Mathematica and, alongside G. E. Moore, led the British 'revolt against idealism.' Who was this founder of analytic philosophy?
Bertrand Russell: English mathematician and philosopher (1872–1970)
Launched in 1993 as a redesigned-wing, glass-cockpit upgrade of an earlier narrow-body jetliner series, this aircraft competes chiefly against the Airbus A320 family — which aircraft is it?
Boeing 737 Next Generation: Single-aisle airliner family.
This volatile red-brown liquid element, with properties between chlorine and iodine, gets its name from the Greek word for 'stench' — which element?
Bromine: Chemical element with atomic number 35 (Br)
Designated Maryland's official state crustacean, this species is expected to benefit from climate change even as overfishing hurts other Chesapeake Bay fisheries — which species?
Callinectes sapidus: Species of crustacean. It is Maryland's largest commercial fishery and has been designated its state crustacean.
A wartime myth claimed eating this vegetable helped British pilots see in the dark — really a cover story for radar — which root vegetable?
Carrot: Root vegetable. The carrot (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) is a root vegetable in the umbellifer family Apiaceae.
Holder of 186 patents, this American engineer ran research at General Motors for nearly three decades and gave the world the electric car starter, leaded gasoline, and Freon — who was he?
Charles F. Kettering: American inventor, engineer and businessman (1876–1958)
Despite its common 'cat' nickname, this small nocturnal mammal from Africa and Asia is not a feline at all — and one African species yields a musky scent long used in perfumery — what is it?
Civet: Mammals of the families Viverridae and Nandiniidae and the genus Fossa.

A member of the true thrushes, this Eurasian songbird whose nominate male is all black breeds across Europe, western Asia, and North Africa and has been introduced to Australia and New Zealand — which bird is it?
Common blackbird: Thrush native to Europe, western Asia and North Africa.
Smelling of vanilla but tasting bitter, which plant compound isn't itself an anticoagulant, though its derivatives inspired the blood-thinning drug warfarin?
This Zambian-born economist turned heads with four New York Times bestsellers, including "Dead Aid," which argues that foreign aid actually holds Africa back. Which author and life peer is it?
Dambisa Moyo, Baroness Moyo: Zambian-born economist (born February 1969)
Known for feigning death when cornered, which genus of cat-sized marsupials includes the only marsupial species found north of Mexico?
Didelphis: Genus of marsupials. The six species in the genus Didelphis, commonly known as Large American opossums, are members of the opossum order, Didelphimorphia.
Nicknamed 'Viking disease,' this hand condition — first surgically treated in 1831 by the surgeon it's named after — permanently curls the ring finger inward. What is it?
Dupuytren's contracture: Medical condition featuring permanent bending of fingers.
This German chess player, mathematician and philosopher held the world title for 27 years — the longest reign ever — partly by a famously "psychological" approach to rattling opponents; who was he?

This branch of zoology studying animal behavior traces its scientific roots to Darwin and came into its own in the 1930s through Nobel laureates Tinbergen, Lorenz, and von Frisch — what's the field called?
Birds of prey in the genus Falco, some small species are called hobbies and hover-hunters are called kestrels — what are they collectively known as?
Falcon: Birds of prey in the genus Falco. The largest falcon is the gyrfalcon at up to 65 cm (26 in) in length.
Members of the order Siphonaptera, these flightless blood-sucking parasites can leap 50 times their own body length — what are they?
Flea: Insects of the order Siphonaptera. Flea, the common name for the order Siphonaptera, includes 2,500 species of small flightless insects that live as external parasites of mammals and birds.
Found in the rainforests and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa, this snake has the longest fangs of any venomous species — up to two inches — and the highest venom yield of any snake — which snake?
Gaboon viper: Species of snake. It is the largest member of the genus Bitis.
Ranging from eastern Bangladesh to Southeast Asia, these tailless 'lesser apes' swing branch to branch at speeds up to 55 km/h (34 mph) — what are they?
Gibbon: Family of apes. The family historically contained one genus, but now is split into four extant genera and 20 species.
The largest and most widespread member of its rosy-pink family, this wading bird ranges from Sub-Saharan Africa to the Mediterranean and Central Asia — which species?
In music theory, this concept for combining different pitches into chords and progressions has both a 'vertical' frequency dimension and a 'horizontal' time dimension — what is it called?
Harmony: Aspect of music. In music, harmony is the concept of combining different sounds in order to create new, distinct musical ideas.
Known scientifically as singultus, this involuntary diaphragm spasm closes the glottis in about 35 milliseconds to produce a signature sound — what reflex is it?
Hiccup: Involuntary contraction of the diaphragm. The rhythm of the hiccup, or the time between hiccups, tends to be relatively constant.

Made of one oxygen and one hydrogen atom bonded together with a negative charge, this ion is the active base in the sodium compound used to produce millions of tons of industrial chemicals yearly. What ion is it?
Patented in 1961 and used to fight fever, pain and inflammation by blocking the cyclooxygenase enzyme, this drug sits on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines — what is it?
Before he proposed that the Earth behaves like one self-regulating living system, this English independent scientist built the detector that first revealed CFCs lurking in our atmosphere. Who was he?
A former Navy SEAL turned physician, this NASA astronaut flew to the International Space Station in 2025 as part of Expedition 72/73 after earning a Silver Star for valor in combat — who is he?
Jonny Kim: American astronaut, physician, and former U.S. Navy SEAL (born 1984)
A German mechanical engineer turned economist, he founded a famous annual gathering of global leaders in 1971 and chaired it until stepping down in 2025. Who is he?
Klaus Schwab: Founder of the World Economic Forum (born 1938)
A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange, this small evergreen tree may have first appeared in northeastern India, and its fruit's juice is about 5–6% citric acid — what is it?

This anatomic form of lung infection causes inflammatory fluid to consolidate across an entire continuous section of one lung, and in children shows up instead as a rounded pattern due to immature air-pore connections — what is it?
Lobar pneumonia: Lung infection. It is one of three anatomic classifications of pneumonia (the other being bronchopneumonia and atypical pneumonia).
A field of artificial intelligence built on statistics and optimization, it develops algorithms that learn from data and handle unseen examples without being explicitly programmed — what is it?
Machine learning: Subset of artificial intelligence. Statistics and mathematical optimisation methods compose the foundations of machine learning.
On April 3, 1973, this Motorola engineer made history's first public call from a handheld cell phone on a Manhattan sidewalk — who is he?
Cataloged as a nebula by a French astronomer in 1781, this supergiant elliptical galaxy boasts roughly 15,000 globular clusters, a hundred times more than our own — which galaxy is it?
Messier 87: Galaxy in the constellation Virgo.

This Serbian polymath — mathematician, astronomer, civil engineer — explained Earth's long-term climate swings by tracking our planet's shifting position relative to the Sun, a theory of cycles that now bears his name. Who was he?
Milutin Milanković: Serbian scientist and professor (1879–1958)
This Bangladeshi economist founded Grameen Bank and pioneered modern microcredit, winning the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize before later leading an interim government — who is he?
Muhammad Yunus: Bangladeshi economist and statesman (born 1940)

The Navy paid his Purdue aeronautical-engineering tuition under the Holloway Plan, and he flew the Grumman F9F Panther off the USS Essex in the Korean War before his most famous flight of all — which Ohio-born aviator was he?
This carnivorous freshwater fish, found widely across cold waters worldwide, has a current all-tackle world record of 25 kg, caught in Germany in 1986 — what species is it?
Northern pike: Species of fish. The northern pike (Esox lucius), also known as jack, northern or simply pike, is a species of carnivorous fish of the genus Esox (pikes).
A woody perennial native to the Mediterranean and a close relative of sweet marjoram, this mint-family herb is a staple of Italian and Greek cooking — what is it?
This term describes the bulk functional tissue of an organ like the brain or lungs, the filler tissue inside flatworms, and certain leaf cross-section layers in plants — what is it?
Parenchyma: Visceral tissue found inside organs of animals.
Often triggered by a ruptured appendix or a perforated gallbladder, this inflammation of the abdominal lining causes severe pain and swelling — what is it?

Peritonitis: Inflammation of abdominal organ lining. Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
This French physicist shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with his wife, making them the first married couple to win a Nobel — who is he?
Pierre Curie: French physicist and chemist (1859–1906)
Also called quaking aspen for the way its leaves flutter in the slightest breeze, which poplar species is native to the Old World's cool temperate regions?
This evergreen shrub or small tree native to South America is pollinated chiefly by the honey bee and gives us a popular tropical fruit — what species is it?
Psidium guajava: Species of flowering plant.
Born from refraction, internal reflection, and dispersion of light in water droplets, this arc always appears in the patch of sky directly opposite the sun — what is it?
Also called vitamin B2, this nutrient forms two key coenzymes for energy metabolism, can be prescribed for corneal thinning, and taken orally may cut down migraines in adults — which vitamin is it?
Riboflavin: Vitamin, dietary supplement, and yellow food dye.

Nicknamed 'The Kite' (or perhaps 'The Dragon'), this Swedish supersonic fighter-interceptor's innovative double-delta wing traces back to 1948 and entered frontline service in March 1960 — which aircraft?
Saab 35 Draken: 1955 Swedish fighter aircraft. The full-scale production version entered service with frontline squadrons of the Swedish Air Force on 8 March 1960.

Named after a colourful terrestrial flower, this predatory marine cnidarian is typically a single polyp anchored to a hard surface — a tentacled relative of coral and jellyfish, but with no medusa stage. What is it?
Sea anemone: Marine animals of the order Actiniaria.
Better known by the brand name Viagra, this drug treats erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension, kicking in within about twenty minutes — what is it?

Sildenafil: Drug for erectile dysfunction and hypertension. Sildenafil, sold under the brand name Viagra among others, is a medication used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
